messages:
sarah: paging oncall — we just got an incident-bot alert for elevated SSE disconnects hitting the streaming gateway (multiple customers). seeing a spike starting ~1967889900. can oncall pick this up? :rotating_light:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED (sev: high) — 173 affected requests/min, 12% error rate for streaming connections. pager escalated to @oncall. logs and traces attached.
oncall: I'm on it. grabbing logs for the last 30m. can someone post any reproducer or customer example?
mike: putting a customer's trace (redacted) here — streaming handshake times out then client retries into a tool-call parse error. users see truncated tool responses. snippet: ```
[stream] handshake start: 1967889921
[stream] handshake timeout after 30s
[toolcall] parse_error: unexpected token '}' at byte 342
[client] UA: AcmeApp/2.1 (iOS)
```
eli: interesting — the parse error looks like the payload includes an extra trailing brace. could be a client-side bug or an intermediate chunking issue causing out-of-order fragments.
sarah: customer-impact check: CS reports 3 customers affected (Acme, Atlas, BetaRetail). CS-bot says two support tickets with screenshots of "partial tool output" and one app crash.
cs-bot: CUSTOMER IMPACT: 3 customers, 27 users total, highest severity customer (Acme) on a paid Dedicated tier.
oncall: quick mitigation idea — force-fallback to batching mode or shorter chunk sizes at the streaming gateway to try to avoid chunk boundary splits. can we toggle that without a deploy?
naveen: we can change gateway config via feature flag for connection fragment-buffering. rolling that now to 20s buffer -> will notify when live.
incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE applied to gateway-nodes-3 via ff:enable fragment-buffering=20s by naveen at 1967890280.
mike: after toggle: immediate drop in parse errors in the next 90s for the traces I was watching. posting sample log: ```
[stream] fragment-buffering=20s applied
[toolcall] parse_error: 0 (previously 12/min)
[client] UA: AcmeApp/2.1
```
oncall: good — still seeing some disconnects but parse errors reduced. we should build a short timeline and hypotheses for the RCA.
sarah: timeline (first pass):
- 1967889900: small increase in streaming handshakes failing (gateway logs show handshake timeouts)
- 1967889921: first customer trace showing handshake then parse error (see above)
- 1967890100: incident-bot alert threshold breached -> pagerescalation
- 1967890280: fragment-buffering flag toggled (mitigation deployed)
- 1967890350: parse errors drop, partial recovery in affected traces
- 1967891200: ongoing elevated p95 latency for some streams (~700ms) but errors largely reduced
(please correct if anyone has additional logs)
eli: adding logs from runtime nodes: ```
[svc-runtime] WARN kvcache: miss spikes during streaming at 1967889895..1967890050
[svc-runtime] ERROR out-of-order-chunk: seq 45 arrived before seq 44 (node grpc connection flapped)
```
mike: client compatibility note — AcmeApp uses an older streaming client that sends small chunks (~128B) and relies on server reassembly. if a gateway node retries or reconnects mid-stream, small chunks may arrive interleaved.
naveen: hypothesis list (in-thread):
1) client fragmentation + gateway retries -> chunk interleaving -> toolcall payload corruption -> parse errors.
2) gateway node flaps (network blips) cause re-orders on the server side due to replaying fragments from different TCP connections.
3) regression in our streaming runtime related to new batching optimizer that attempted aggressive chunk coalescing. (low confidence)
4) client-side bug producing an extra brace under rare conditions (needs customer repro).

eli: marking hypothesis 1 as highest likelihood based on out-of-order-chunk errors in runtime logs and reduction after fragment-buffering.
oncall: next steps for live RCA:
- collect per-node conn logs (+ grpc debug) from 1967889800..1967891400 (eli action)
- request customer repro traces from Acme and Atlas (cs will request, sarah follow-up)
- run load test to reproduce small-chunk fragmentation + synthetic gateway retry (mike)
- run bisect against recent batching optimizer changes (naveen + eng-runtime)

sarah: I've queued a customer message draft for Acme: "We're investigating streaming interruptions that may cause partial tool responses. Could you share a reproducible trace or app logs around the time of failure? We'll prioritize." cs-bot queued ticket updates.
cs-bot: TICKET UPDATE: Acme assigned to CS-Eli, priority P0 for Dedicated customer.
mike: immediate workaround suggestion for prod: enable reverse-proxy keepalive tuning to reduce gateway reconnections. this is lower-risk than rolling back runtime.
naveen: we can flip keepalive for the proxy layer in 2min, applying to edge-proxies only to reduce reconnections. proceeding.
incident-bot: CHANGE: keepalive-tune applied edge-proxy cluster by naveen at 1967890600.
eli: after keepalive change — p50/p95 connection stability improved; still monitoring for any new parse events. logs show much lower out-of-order-chunk counts.
oncall: good. document mitigation timeline in the incident doc and hand off to oncall->eng-runtime for full RCA.
sarah: handoff: @naveen and @eli to lead the root cause analysis. oncall will close the incident when errors are below normal for 1 hour and customer updates are sent.
mike: notes for RCA write-up: include customer UA matrix, gateway node mapping, example corrupted payloads (redacted), and hypothesis ranking with confidence levels. also capture config diffs around the recent batching optimizer.
eli: I'll start the RCA doc skeleton in the incidents drive and link here when ready. uploading initial artifacts and per-node logs.
sarah: thanks everyone. tagging a few action items in-thread: 
- eli: collect and upload node logs (done -> link: https://drive.internal/incidents/1967890123/nodelogs)
- mike: reproduce with small-chunk load test (in progress)
- naveen: bisect runtime changes + config diffs
- oncall: monitor for 1h post-mitigation

oncall: closing note: mitigation appears effective; readiness to rollback runtime if bisect shows a clear regression. keeping the thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
